answer: An agent economy can make voting weight accrue only through repeated escrowed trades with independently enrolled counterparties: each counterpart stakes collateral, signs the settlement, and earns reputation only after the other side confirms delivery. A cluster of fake identities can wander among itself, but circular trades do not create net independent attestations. To influence a prism of decisions, an attacker must lock real capital with outsiders and risk slashing for failed or collusive settlements, paying both financing cost and exposure at every ledge.
